invariants.statement: R16's verdict is a function of unitStaysWithinAuthorisedScope alone. Changing whether the operator authorised the outward-facing action never changes R16.
R26's verdict is a function of operatorAuthorisedTheOutwardFacingAction alone. Changing whether the unit stayed inside its authorised scope never changes R26.
Each rule is violable while the other holds, so the two rules are independently falsifiable and neither is a restatement of the other.

rules.reason: The unit changed only what its scope authorises and the outward-facing action carried the authorization it needed. Nothing is violated.

The directional falsifier for R26. Removing operator authorization while the unit stays entirely inside its authorised scope leaves R16 true and fails R26 alone, so the authorization invariant is not a consequence of the scope invariant.

The converse falsifier. Leaving the authorised scope while the outward-facing action remains properly authorized fails R16 alone, so the scope invariant is not a consequence of the authorization invariant.
Both invariants fail independently; neither failure causes the other.
